guidelines.title: Breast Cancer Screening
guidelines.recommendation: Screen with mammography every 2 years for women aged 40-74.
guidelines.notes: Decision to start before 40 should be individualized, especially for those with family history or known BRCA mutations. Women aged 75+ have insufficient evidence (I statement).

guidelines.title: Cervical Cancer Screening
guidelines.recommendation: Screen with cytology (Pap smear) every 3 years for ages 21-29. For ages 30-65, screen with cytology every 3 years, hrHPV testing every 5 years, or co-testing every 5 years.
guidelines.frequency: Every 3 years (cytology) or every 5 years (hrHPV or co-testing for ages 30-65)
guidelines.notes: Not recommended for women <21, women >65 with adequate prior screening, or those who have had a hysterectomy with removal of the cervix and no history of high-grade precancerous lesion or cervical cancer.

guidelines.title: Colorectal Cancer Screening
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for colorectal cancer using stool-based tests (FIT annually, FIT-DNA every 1-3 years), colonoscopy every 10 years, CT colonography every 5 years, or flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years.
guidelines.notes: Grade B for ages 76-85 (selective screening based on overall health and prior screening history). Earlier and more frequent screening for high-risk individuals (family history, IBD, hereditary syndromes).

guidelines.title: Lung Cancer Screening
guidelines.population: Adults aged 50-80 with >= 20 pack-year smoking history who currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years
guidelines.recommendation: Annual screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT).
riskFactors: current smoker or quit within 15 years
guidelines.notes: Discontinue once a person has not smoked for 15 years or develops a health problem that substantially limits life expectancy or willingness to have curative lung surgery.

guidelines.title: Prostate Cancer Screening
guidelines.recommendation: The decision to be screened with PSA should be an individual one, informed by shared decision-making about potential benefits and harms.
guidelines.notes: Grade D for men 70+. African American men and those with family history may benefit from earlier discussion (age 40-55).

guidelines.title: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Screening
guidelines.population: Men aged 65-75 who have ever smoked
guidelines.recommendation: One-time screening with ultrasonography.
guidelines.notes: Grade C for men 65-75 who have never smoked (selective screening). Grade I for women who have never smoked. Grade I for women who have ever smoked.

guidelines.title: Hypertension Screening
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for hypertension with office blood pressure measurement. Obtain measurements outside of the clinical setting for diagnostic confirmation before starting treatment.
guidelines.frequency: Annually (at minimum); more frequently if elevated
guidelines.notes: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is the reference standard for confirming the diagnosis.

guidelines.title: Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes Screening
guidelines.population: Adults aged 35-70 who are overweight or obese
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes. Refer patients with prediabetes to effective preventive interventions.
guidelines.notes: ADA recommends screening all adults starting at age 35, or earlier if BMI >= 25 (>= 23 in Asian Americans) with one or more additional risk factors.

guidelines.title: Statin Use for Primary Prevention of CVD
guidelines.population: Adults aged 40-75 with 1+ CVD risk factor and 10-year ASCVD risk >= 10%
guidelines.recommendation: Prescribe a statin for the primary prevention of CVD in adults aged 40-75 who have one or more cardiovascular risk factors (dyslipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, or smoking) and an estimated 10-year ASCVD risk of 10% or greater.
guidelines.notes: Grade C for adults with 10-year risk 7.5-10%. Insufficient evidence for adults over 76.

guidelines.title: Depression Screening in Adults
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for depression in the general adult population, including pregnant and postpartum persons.
guidelines.frequency: Periodically (no specific interval; many practices screen annually or at each visit)
guidelines.notes: Screening should be implemented with adequate systems in place to ensure accurate diagnosis, effective treatment, and appropriate follow-up. PHQ-9 is a commonly used validated tool.

guidelines.title: Anxiety Screening in Adults
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for anxiety disorders in adults aged 18-64, including pregnant and postpartum persons.
guidelines.notes: Insufficient evidence (I statement) for adults 65+. GAD-7 is a commonly used screening tool.

guidelines.title: Hepatitis C Virus Infection Screening
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in adults aged 18 to 79 years.
guidelines.frequency: One-time (universal); periodic for ongoing risk factors
guidelines.notes: Universal one-time screening. Periodic screening for those with ongoing risk factors (injection drug use, etc.).

guidelines.title: Hepatitis B Virus Infection Screening
guidelines.population: Adolescents and adults at increased risk
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for hepatitis B virus infection in adolescents and adults at increased risk for infection.
guidelines.frequency: One-time for at-risk populations; periodic for ongoing risk
guidelines.notes: Risk groups include persons born in countries with HBV prevalence >= 2%, US-born persons not vaccinated as infants whose parents were born in regions with HBV prevalence >= 8%, and HIV-positive persons.

guidelines.title: HIV Screening
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for HIV infection in all adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65 years. Also screen younger and older persons at increased risk.
guidelines.frequency: At least once; more frequently for those at increased risk
guidelines.notes: At least one-time screening for all. More frequent screening (e.g., annually) for those at increased risk (MSM, injection drug use, transactional sex).

guidelines.title: Osteoporosis Screening
guidelines.population: Women aged 65+ and postmenopausal women <65 at increased risk
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for osteoporosis with bone measurement testing (DEXA) to prevent osteoporotic fractures in women 65+ and in postmenopausal women younger than 65 who are at increased risk of osteoporosis.
guidelines.frequency: At least once starting at age 65; interval uncertain (typically every 2-5 years based on T-score)
guidelines.notes: Insufficient evidence (I statement) for screening men. FRAX tool can help identify younger postmenopausal women at increased risk.

guidelines.title: Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults
guidelines.population: Adults aged 65+ at increased risk for falls
guidelines.recommendation: Provide exercise interventions to prevent falls in community-dwelling adults 65 years and older who are at increased risk for falls.
guidelines.notes: Exercise interventions that include gait, balance, and functional training components are the most effective.

guidelines.title: Unhealthy Alcohol Use Screening and Counseling
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for unhealthy alcohol use in primary care and provide persons engaged in risky or hazardous drinking with brief behavioral counseling interventions.
guidelines.notes: AUDIT-C is a commonly used validated screening tool. Brief interventions (5-15 minutes) are effective.

guidelines.title: Tobacco Use Counseling and Interventions
guidelines.recommendation: Ask all adults about tobacco use, advise them to stop using tobacco, and provide behavioral interventions and FDA-approved pharmacotherapy for cessation.
guidelines.notes: FDA-approved pharmacotherapies include nicotine replacement therapy (patch, gum, lozenge, inhaler, nasal spray), bupropion SR, and varenicline. Combination therapy (behavioral + pharmacotherapy) most effective.

guidelines.title: Weight Loss to Prevent Obesity-Related Morbidity
guidelines.recommendation: Offer or refer adults with a BMI of 30 or higher to intensive, multicomponent behavioral interventions.
guidelines.frequency: Screen at every visit; behavioral interventions are typically 12-26 sessions over 12 months
guidelines.notes: Intensive behavioral interventions include multiple contacts, goal setting, improving diet and physical activity, self-monitoring, and addressing barriers to change.

guidelines.title: Aspirin Use to Prevent CVD
guidelines.recommendation: The decision to initiate low-dose aspirin for primary prevention of CVD in adults aged 40-59 with >= 10% 10-year ASCVD risk should be an individual one. Evidence indicates a small net benefit.
guidelines.notes: Grade D for adults 60+: do not initiate aspirin for primary CVD prevention. Does not apply to secondary prevention (established CVD).

guidelines.title: Chlamydia and Gonorrhea Screening
guidelines.population: Sexually active women aged 24 and younger, and older women at increased risk
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for chlamydia and gonorrhea in sexually active women 24 years and younger, and in older women who are at increased risk for infection.
guidelines.notes: Insufficient evidence (I statement) for screening men. NAAT is the preferred testing method.

guidelines.title: Skin Cancer Prevention Counseling
guidelines.population: Young adults aged 6 months to 24 years with fair skin
guidelines.recommendation: Counsel young adults, adolescents, children, and parents of young children about minimizing exposure to ultraviolet radiation to reduce risk of skin cancer.
guidelines.notes: Insufficient evidence for adults over 24 with fair skin. No recommendation for skin cancer screening with total body skin exam.

guidelines.title: Vitamin D Supplementation to Prevent Falls
guidelines.recommendation: Do not use vitamin D supplementation to prevent falls in community-dwelling adults 65 years and older.
guidelines.notes: This applies to primary prevention of falls. Vitamin D for treatment of deficiency or osteoporosis is a separate clinical question.

guidelines.title: Interventions for Prediabetes to Prevent Type 2 Diabetes
guidelines.recommendation: Offer or refer adults with prediabetes to effective preventive interventions (e.g., Diabetes Prevention Program-modeled intensive behavioral counseling focused on diet and physical activity).
guidelines.frequency: Intensive lifestyle intervention (typically 16+ sessions over 6 months with maintenance)
guidelines.notes: Diabetes Prevention Program demonstrated 58% reduction in diabetes incidence with intensive lifestyle modification vs 31% with metformin.

guidelines.title: Vision Screening in Older Adults
guidelines.recommendation: Current evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening for impaired visual acuity in older adults.
guidelines.notes: Despite I statement, many professional organizations (AAO, AOA) recommend comprehensive eye exams every 1-2 years for adults 65+.

guidelines.title: Hearing Loss Screening in Older Adults
guidelines.recommendation: Screen for hearing loss in adults 50 years and older.
guidelines.notes: Screening can be done with validated questionnaires (e.g., Hearing Handicap Inventory for the Elderly) or audiometry.

guidelines.title: Cognitive Impairment Screening in Older Adults
guidelines.recommendation: Current evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening for cognitive impairment in older adults.
guidelines.notes: Despite I statement, the Alzheimer's Association recommends that clinicians be alert to cognitive changes and evaluate when concerns arise. Medicare AWV includes cognitive assessment.
